page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2861.88 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is limited, with stress-ng multi-core (5736.38) and Geekbench multi-core (4153.0) scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained; read-only memory bandwidth for small blocks is 282.38 GB/sec, and large-block write bandwidth drops to 15.16 GB/sec, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression (27.54 GB/sec) and Passmark CPU (7047.04) scores represent average tier performance.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c3d-standard-4 is defined by its dedicated AMD EPYC hardware class and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, offering a stable entry point for workloads that require dedicated compute resources without the overhead of larger instances. However, users face tradeoffs: while single-threaded execution is highly capable, the instance is less efficient for memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks, multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale database operations, as evidenced by weak Passmark database and static web serving throughput. It is best suited for light general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-intensity LLM inference using small models.
